route: scripted (procedural Blender geometry; no provider generation; face art reused from the P5-T6 UI atlas)

texturesSampled: ui/dice-d6 (shared UI atlas page, resident for the UI)

lods: LOD0 only: a 40 mm die stays under 700 triangles, so a LOD chain saves nothing measurable
bake: none: face art is the shared atlas page and brass is a factor (or the shared brass-polished set), so nothing is baked

frame.convention: src/dice/faces.ts die-local frame; identity orientation = DicePresenter's
frame.uv: TEXCOORD_0 is glTF (v down); loadDice flips v once so face UVs are in the UI atlas's bottom-left texture space

materialsUsed: factor-only polished brass named after the approved P4-T3 brass-polished set (bindable at runtime); the face slot samples the shared P5-T6 UI atlas page
license: Original work generated in Blender from a checked-in script; face art and style reference from Paul's paid Higgsfield plan (Terms of Use 4.4)

checks: face table (GLB extras and manifest) equals faces.ts and content/dice.ts
reimport gate (face-up UVs in the atlas cell, no mirrored UVs, Blender reimport)

approvals.notes: validate-generated-assets verdict is reported to the orchestrator, not self-recorded
original procedural geometry; face art from the P5-T6 atlas (its own provenance)
Paul approves the in-engine look (docs/blender-kit-project.md ruling 3)
blender-kit-pieces requires an independent >= 80/100 score; unscored means unaccepted

independentScore.scale: 0-100 visual fidelity to the art direction
independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the asset)

rubric.note: Unchanged since the last score (25). This is still a rounded brass cube with a raised frame around inset walnut faces, and it matches the proportions of L-board-1 panel 4. Points are lost because the reference sets its faces in a recessed, dark-bevelled well. Here the frame steps straight down to walnut: a scan at y=300 across the right die's top-face inner edge (x 512 to 538) falls from relL 0.200 to 0.065 over about 10 px with no dark lip, so the faces read nearly flush.

Up 2 from 16. Commit e2a9530 makes the pips emissive. The brightest 1% of pip pixels now reach #FEEAC7 (relL 0.84), and the pips are the brightest element on both dice. They glow cream-peach rather than candle amber: the median is #CFB795 (H35, S 0.28), and saturation tops out at 0.40 across all pip pixels. The reference pip cores measure #FFD848 (S 0.72). The pips are still flat discs with a tan ring (#958255), not recessed cups. A ring sampled just outside the centre pip (relL 0.098) sits inside the walnut's own grain range (0.054 to 0.096), so the glow does not spill onto the face the way panel 4 does. The brass body, walnut faces and correct pip layout are all present.

Unchanged (12). The walnut atlas grain is painterly and strong. The brass is still uniform, with no edge wear and no value breakup. Under a hue mask (H38 to 60), brass relL runs p10 0.143, p50 0.167 and p90 0.240, a narrow band. The only real highlight is the rounded top-front lip (#8B794B to #B39F71). On the right die in p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg it reads as smooth olive-gold plastic.

Up 1 from 9. Commit 02e65a1 lands the walnut: top-face walnut is #5E3F2D (H22, S 0.52) and front-face walnut #573826. Across the six lineup dice it measures #5B3D2C to #60412E, against the bible's #583C26 (H26, S 0.57). Before the change it was hue 15 to 21. The brass is still dull and olive. The hue-masked median is #826F48 (H40, S 0.45, V 0.51) and the top 5% is #B39F71 (S 0.37), against palette #DEC16A (V 0.87) and the reference's lit brass #EEB249 (S 0.69). The pip hue is right (H35 against candle amber H37), but saturation is about half (S 0.28 against 0.58). The value structure (light frame, dark face, bright pips) is correct.

Down 1 from 9. Pip-to-walnut contrast measures 4.9:1 on the right die's top face and 5.5:1 on its front face, and 4.6 to 4.9:1 on the six lineup dice. The last score had 6.3:1, but from an in-game tray shot under different light, so the delta is approximate. Part of the drop comes from the requested walnut grade, which lifted walnut to relL 0.06. The pips stay countable: the centre pip spans 35 px at this framing, and the emissive keeps them lit in dim light. This is still below the reference's roughly 10:1 (pip #FFD848 on face #3D2212), and the evidence is desktop only.

topFixes: Change the pip emissive colour and map from cream to saturated candle amber: a core near #FFD848 or #F3BE65 with S of at least 0.6. If tone mapping still washes it out, lower emissiveIntensity from 1.8 to about 1.0 to 1.2, or add selective bloom. More intensity on the current cream map only pushes it toward white (the brightest 1% is already #FEEAC7 at S 0.22).

Recess each pip into a shallow cup with a dark warm-black (#231D1A) rim so it reads as a lit well, as in panel 4, and add a soft amber glow ring baked into the walnut atlas around each pip (currently no measurable spill: 0.098 against grain 0.054 to 0.096).

Give the brass body value and wear: use the approved polished-brass texture set, or add edge-wear and cavity-darkening masks so brass relL spans about 0.08 to 0.5, not 0.14 to 0.24. Lift the lit midtone toward #DEC16A (from #826F48) so it reads as polished brass, not olive plastic.
Add a dark bevelled lip (about 2 to 3 mm, near #231D1A) where the frame steps down to the walnut so the faces sit in a recessed well instead of reading flush.
independentScore.method: Independent reviewer (did not build the asset). I read the dice and palette sections of docs/art-bible.md and the previous independentScore in assets-source/dice/brass-d6/provenance.json, and did not open any author self-score or fidelity file. Primary evidence was the in-engine renders of the shipped HEAD in /tmp/rxr-prev/dice-shipped-shots/: p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg and p5-dice-brass-d6-lineup.jpg, both 960x640. The reference was L-board-1.png panel 4, cropped at (60,956)-(750,1490). Measurements used Pillow under python3 -I: median sRGB in fixed crop boxes, with pips segmented at relL above 0.45, walnut at relL below 0.08 and brass by hue mask (H38 to 60, S above 0.3). Contrast ratios are WCAG (relL+0.05)/(relL+0.05), and I sampled the frame-to-face transition and the area around one pip. Floor-contaminated rectangles were discarded. The deltas against the last score (71) are approximate, because that score's contrast figures came from in-game tray shots with a darker floor and different light. All evidence is desktop (Apple M4, ANGLE Metal) with no headset capture. Date 2026-11-16.
